comment: Preflight verification contract for the T-005 quality gate, authored by the coder session preparing this task for gate review (T-004's contract is the schema this one matches; risk/required_workflow/stack/spec_revision follow its own pattern exactly). Every check started at passes=false and was flipped only after this session RAN its command at the current HEAD and inspected the saved output -- the implementation report (reports/implementation/epic-195-a7-compatibility/T-005.md) was treated as a claim, not trusted outright. Every passing check's evidence field points at a coder-*.log this session produced fresh under specs/epic-195-a7-compatibility/verification/T-005/, never at an implementer-authored log, with one deliberate exception: red_evidence/green_evidence on the tdd-required unit-tests/acceptance-tests rows point at the implementer's own red-sh.log/red-ps1.log/green-sh.log/green-ps1.log, because those RED captures were reconstructed by the T-005 implementation session via a scratch-copy technique (45dda57f^ driver/registry content + current tests) that this session independently re-verified rather than re-executed -- a RED capture made honest after the fact by re-running it now would be GREEN, since the fix already exists in the tree, so re-creating it would manufacture a false artifact. Risk high and Required Workflow tdd are transcribed from tasks.md#T-005 (Security Boundary B2: tests/loops/loop-inventory.json, tests/lib/loop-driver.{sh,ps1}). ADDENDUM (2026-08-20, cross-model panelist remediation): the original regression check's evidence (coder-regression.log, still present, unedited) enumerated consumers via 'grep -l loop-driver.sh tests/*.tests.sh' -- a .sh-only glob that could not match tests/lib/loop-driver.ps1's own consumers, and separately missed one real .sh consumer (tests/hitl-wfi-terminal.tests.sh). The regression check now points at coder-regression-both-runtimes.log, which enumerates every suite that genuinely dot-sources tests/lib/loop-driver.{sh,ps1} (5 per runtime: hitl-wfi-terminal, loop-consistency, loop-driver, loop-escalation, loop-inventory) and records all 10 runs green in both runtimes. SEPARATE, UNRESOLVED FINDING (2026-08-20, same panelist, this session's own investigation): the panelist correctly found that the recorded producer identity 'done-transition:assert-terminal' (design.md's per-kind producer table, line ~248) names a call site inside assert_terminal that cannot exist -- T-005's own Done When ('assert_terminal ... byte-identical to their pre-task form', locked by TEST-009.2/TEST-009.3 in tests/loop-inventory.tests.{sh,ps1}) and AC-009 (acceptance-tests.md: 'assert_terminal/assert_artifacts_schema remain unmodified') together make that call site permanently unimplementable, and T-006/T-007's own suites in fact emit the event from the test case itself, immediately after assert_terminal succeeds (documented at tests/loop-consistency.tests.sh:30-35, tests/loop-escalation.tests.sh:67-72, and reports/implementation/epic-195-a7-compatibility/T-006.md's own 'Specification Differences' item 2, which mechanically verified that wiring the call inside assert_terminal trips TEST-009.2 red). Both routes to closing this are blocked by frozen, hash-bound Phase 1 documents (tasks.md:19-27: 'design.md ... acceptance-tests.md ... those are frozen, hash-bound Phase 1 artifacts'): (a) correcting the recorded producer identity to name the real call site is blocked by design.md's own per-kind producer table (line 248, 'assert_terminal's own comparison call') read together with design.md:239-240 ('producer is a required, identity-compared field of every event -- never documentation-only prose a future implementer could satisfy with any arbitrary string') -- renaming the identity to a test-case call site would contradict that specific, normative, frozen table entry, which is drift, not a fix; (b) adding the call inside assert_terminal is blocked by acceptance-tests.md's own frozen AC-009 row ('assert_terminal/assert_artifacts_schema remain unmodified') and by design.md's own Constraint Compliance table (line 1103, 'assert_terminal/assert_artifacts_schema unmodified (AC-009)'). Neither route is available without editing a frozen document, which is out of scope for a coder session; this is reported as an open finding, not resolved by this contract or any code change in this session.

checks.waiver_reason: stack: shell -- T-005's deliverables are tests/loops/loop-inventory.json (a JSON registry) and the POSIX-shell/PowerShell twins tests/lib/loop-driver.{sh,ps1}/tests/loop-inventory.tests.{sh,ps1}. This repository configures no shell linter and no JSON linter (no shellcheck, no PSScriptAnalyzer, no jsonlint invocation in tests/run-all.{sh,ps1} or .github/workflows/test.yml), so there is no lint command whose output could be recorded. risk-gate-matrix.md Stack descriptor.

stack: shell -- shell and PowerShell are untyped and this repository configures no static type-check command for either runtime. tests/loops/loop-inventory.json's shape (including the new, additive capability_applicability field) is enforced by TEST-008's own schema-validation assertions in tests/loop-inventory.tests.{sh,ps1}, not by a type checker. risk-gate-matrix.md Stack descriptor.

No service or network integration is in T-005's scope. The one cross-process interaction -- tests/loop-inventory.tests.{sh,ps1} reading the registry and driving the new driver functions through jq/ConvertFrom-Json -- is exercised end to end by the acceptance run, not by a separate integration layer.

stack: shell -- no compile or bundle step exists for shell/PowerShell scripts and a JSON registry; there is no dist/ artifact and design.md's Deployment / CI Plan records no build obligation for this task. risk-gate-matrix.md Stack descriptor.

No independently startable application, service, or UI. T-005's deliverable is a registry field plus library functions consumed by a batch test suite; the acceptance run invokes both entry points for real in both runtimes, so a separate smoke run would duplicate the acceptance evidence rather than add to it.

No baseline-behavior.md exists for this feature and T-005 is additive tooling (an optional, additive registry field and new, independent driver functions) rather than a change to existing behavior, so no differential obligation attaches (references/differential-test-policy.md). assert_terminal/assert_artifacts_schema byte-identity is verified directly (Done When), which is a stronger, task-specific guarantee than a generic differential baseline would add.
No user-facing UI surface. traceability.md's Layer Coverage records UX and Frontend as reasoned N/A for the whole feature: 'no GUI, view, dialog, menu item, or human interactive shell surface'.

ds_profile: none -- this repository carries no design-system/ directory and T-005 touches no UI-layer file, so check-design-system's warn-phase conditional control does not activate (risk-gate-matrix.md footnote 4).
